sources.entry: Ghost - Just a blogging platform. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs
Ghost | Professional publishing platform for blogs, newsletters and memberships

summary.one_liner: Ghost is an open-source blogging and publishing platform built on Node.js, released under the MIT license by the Ghost Foundation.
summary.what_it_does: The README introduces Ghost as a publishing platform and points to a CLI tool (ghost-cli, installed via npm) as the recommended way to run a self-hosted instance. The command "ghost install local" sets up a local instance, while "ghost install" performs a server install with automatic SSL via Let's Encrypt. The README says official documentation covers recommended hosting stack, upgrading Ghost, building themes, and working with the API. It also links to a contributing guide and codebase documentation for the monorepo. The README promotes the managed Ghost(Pro) hosting service as the easiest production option, and it mentions a community forum and a changelog newsletter for support and updates.
use_cases: run a publishing site for newsletters
set up a membership or subscription website
use the Ghost API for content
notable: Official ghost-cli installer handles local and production setup
Automatic SSL via Let's Encrypt on server installs
Supports blogs, newsletters and memberships per the awesome-selfhost-docker listing
Developed and funded by the non-profit Ghost Foundation
Theme development and a public API are documented
caveats: The README steers most users toward the paid Ghost(Pro) managed service for production
Self-hosting requires setting up a server and hosting stack; the README points to external docs for recommended setup
Ghost and its logo are trademarks, with a separate trademark policy for usage
